title: SLO Evidence Blackbox Index and Replay Tooling Guide
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary
-------
This page defines the SLO evidence blackbox index (EvIndex) schema, indexing conventions, retention rules, and the standardized replay tooling and runbook used by SRE to reproduce and validate incidents against SLOs. The guide focuses on model-serving stacks (runtime-service, inference-router, kv-cache-proxy, batch-worker) but the patterns are applicable to other inference-adjacent services.

Goals
- Create a single, searchable index of incident evidence artifacts tied to SLOs and capacity signals.
- Provide deterministic replay tooling for latency and correctness regressions.
- Reduce time-to-action for oncall by standardizing artifact collection, verification, and replay steps.
- Make capacity-impacting incidents reproducible in a safe, isolated environment.

Scope
- Services: runtime-service, inference-router, kv-cache-proxy, batch-worker, sla-monitoring, telemetry-pipeline (slo-ingest).
- Evidence types: request traces, token-level latency traces, model KV-cache snapshots, container/GPU metrics, driver logs, routing decisions, config diffs, and sampled payloads.
- Excludes: customer PII payloads (see Data Handling section).

Ownership and SLAs
- EvIndex service owner: eng-sre/operational-tooling.
- Replay infra owner: eng-serving-runtime/team.
- SLA for EvIndex indexing latency: index ingest & availability within 10 minutes for high-severity incidents.
- Oncall escalation: see Runbook -> Step 7.

EvIndex schema (recommended)
- id: string (uuid)
- incident_id: string (JIRA or incident id)
- service: string (runtime-service, inference-router, etc.)
- slo_tag: string (e.g., latency/p95/200ms, availability/99.95%)
- severity: string (sev1|sev2|sev3)
- event_time: ISO8601 timestamp
- collected_by: string (evindex-collector | telemetry-pipeline | manual)
- artifacts: list of artifact ids (ev:trace:..., ev:kvcache:..., ev:container-metrics:... )
- fingerprint: string (sha256 of canonicalized context)

EvIndex example (YAML)
```
id: "ev-3f2c9d"
incident_id: "INC-2026-1349"
service: "runtime-service"
slo_tag: "latency/p95/200ms"
severity: "sev2"
event_time: "2026-02-14T18:22:10Z"
collected_by: "evindex-collector"
artifacts:
  - "ev:trace:3f2c9d"
  - "ev:kvcache:3f2c9d"
  - "ev:gpu-metrics:3f2c9d"
fingerprint: "sha256:ab8df..."
```

Artifact types and retention
- ev:trace:<id> — Full trace (sampled) with token-level events. Retention: 90 days for sev1/2, 30 days for sev3.
- ev:kvcache:<id> — Serialized KV cache snapshot (metadata only + hash) and optional partial dump for replay. Retention: 30 days.
- ev:gpu-metrics:<id> — time-series for GPU utilization, memory, evicted pages. Retention: 180 days.
- ev:container-logs:<id> — logs with structured JSON lines. Retention: 90 days.
- ev:config-diff:<id> — config before/after (redacted). Retention: 365 days.

Data handling and redaction
- Do NOT store customer PII in EvIndex. The collector performs automated redaction: remove text fields matching email/SSN patterns, redact full user messages beyond first 128 chars unless a redaction waiver exists.
- For compliance-sensitive incidents, mark EvIndex entry with confidentiality:restricted and follow eng-sre/security incident evidence procedures.

Indexing pipeline overview
1) Collector (evindex-collector) pulls from telemetry-pipeline (slo-ingest), trace-archiver, and runtime-service sidecars.
2) Collector runs normalization, canonicalization (deterministic ordering of headers, masked fields), and computes fingerprint.
3) Artifacts are uploaded to artifact-store and an EvIndex document is created in EvIndex DB (searchable via Kibana/SeaGlass).
4) Alerts and internal channels (Slack #sre-evindex) are annotated automatically with EvIndex link.

Searchable fields (EvIndex UI)
- incident_id, service, slo_tag, severity, event_time range, fingerprint, artifact types, owner, label tags.

Replay environment (ReplayLab)
- Purpose: run deterministic playback of requests and partial state (KV cache, model seeds) against a sandbox copy of runtime-service.
- Components: replay-runner, state-injector, workload-synthesizer, traffic-mocking gateway, ephemeral GPU pool (replay-gpu-pool), ticketing-hook.

Replay inputs required
- artifact: ev:trace:<id> (request sequence)
- optional artifact: ev:kvcache:<id> (KV snapshot metadata + partial dump)
- runtime image tag (from evindex config-diff)
- target config override (routing, batching, quantization)

Replay safety checklist (must pass before run)
1) Is the incident marked confidentiality:restricted? If yes, get approval from security lead.
2) Does the trace contain PII? If yes, use redacted trace or request waivers.
3) Is the replay-gpu-pool tagged for isolated tenants? (yes by default).
4) Has the replay payload been fuzzed to remove external URLs or callbacks?

Runbook: Reproduce latency regression in ReplayLab (step-by-step)
1) Create EvIndex entry or pull existing: ev = ev-<id>. Confirm artifacts available.
2) Spin up ReplayLab: `./infra/replayctl start --workspace ev-3f2c9d --tag replay-2026-02-18`
3) Inject state (if available): `replayctl inject --kv ev:kvcache:3f2c9d --service runtime-service`
4) Configure target runtime image and config overrides: edit replay-config.yaml (example below).
5) Run a dry-run validation: `replayctl validate --ev ev-3f2c9d` (checks schema, redaction, fingerprint match).
6) Execute replay against isolated GPU pool with telemetry enabled: `replayctl run --ev ev-3f2c9d --capture`
7) After run completes, collect replay artifacts into EvIndex as ev:replay:<id> and attach synthesized telemetry.
8) Compare metrics: p95, p99 latency, error-rate, GPU stalls. Use `ev-compare` tool: `ev-compare --baseline ev:trace:3f2c9d --replay ev:replay:3f2c9d --metrics p95,p99,errors`
9) Document findings into incident ticket and link EvIndex entry. If replay reproduces SLO breach, escalate to oncall and open remediation JIRA with priority based on severity.

Example replay-config.yaml
```
service: runtime-service
image: docker.redwood.ai/runtime-service:2026-02-14-rc3
overrides:
  batching.max_batch_ms: 12
  scheduler.kv_cache_mode: partial-replay
  quantization.profile: q8_2026
replay:
  sample_rate: 1.0
  concurrency: 8
  capture_telemetry: true
```

Acceptance criteria for a successful replay
- The replay run completes without container OOMs (memory < 85% avg).
- Observed p95 latency in replay matches production trace within +/-10%.
- Error rate differential <= 0.5 percentage points.
- If KV-cache used, cache hit rate delta <= 5 percentage points.

Telemetry and automated comparison expectations
- Telemetry-pipeline (slo-ingest) computes canonical metrics for traces and replay runs and stores a summary in EvIndex: {p50, p95, p99, error_rate, gpu_stalls, kv_hit_rate}.
- `ev-compare` outputs a signed JSON summary and a human-readable diff.

Escalation and remediation workflow (when replay reproduces breach)
1) Create remediation issue with labels: incident, reproduce-verified, slo-impact.
2) Assign to owning service oncall and add eng-sre/operational-tooling as watcher.
3) If root cause involves capacity (GPU saturation, network egress), open capacity-topup ticket and assign to eng-sre/capacity-planning.
4) If config regression suspected, open rollback request referencing ev:config-diff.
5) Plan a canary rollout with measured SLO and observe for 24 hours post-fix.

Automation hooks and integration points
- Slack: #sre-evindex posts automated summary with EvIndex link for sev1/2 incidents.
- PagerDuty: Attach EvIndex id to PD event payload.
- Jira: Helper script `ev-jira-create --ev ev-3f2c9d --type remediation` to scaffold issue with artifacts attached.
- CI: replay-runner integration test: `make test-replay` runs a suite of synthetic replays nightly (regresses on p95 drift >5%).

Observability and KPIs for EvIndex & ReplayLab
- Indexing latency (target < 10 minutes for sev1/2).
- Replay turnaround (time from EvIndex link to completed replay): target < 4 hours for sev1, < 24 hours for sev2.
- Reproducibility rate: percent of replays that reproduce the observed SLO breach (target > 65% for sev1 incidents).
- False positive rate of replay diffs (target < 10%).

Common troubleshooting patterns
- If replay p95 >> production p95 but GPU metrics low: verify scheduler and batching flags; ensure concurrency matches production traffic shaping.
- If replay OOMs: reduce replay concurrency and enable partial KV snapshot injection.
- If artifact missing: use `evindex-recover --incident INC-...` to attempt secondary retrieval from trace-archive or sidecar logs.

Rollout plan for EvIndex & ReplayLab (6 weeks)
1) Week 0-1: Feature flagged EvIndex collector deployed to staging; synthetic incidents run nightly.
2) Week 2: Integrate EvIndex posting into existing incident automation for sev1 in staging.
3) Week 3: Soft launch to production for sev2 only; monitoring of indexing latency and integrity.
4) Week 4-5: Enable replay-runner in canary accounts (non-customer data).
5) Week 6: Full rollout for sev1/2 with training and runbook walkthrough.

Operational runbook snippets (quick commands)
- Start a replay workspace:
  `./infra/replayctl start --workspace ev-3f2c9d --pool replay-gpu-pool-01`
- Validate artifacts present:
  `evindex-cli get ev-3f2c9d --show-artifacts`
- Trigger a canned comparison and open JIRA:
  `ev-compare --baseline ev:trace:3f2c9d --replay ev:replay:3f2c9d --out summary.json && ev-jira-create --file summary.json`

Training and runbook playbacks
- Runbook owners must run quarterly tabletop exercises using ReplayLab. Each exercise should include at least one sev2 scenario and 1 synthetic capacity regression.
- Engineers rotating into oncall must complete replay-runner lab: reproduce a seeded p95 regression and file a remediation ticket.

Appendix: Example ev-compare output (truncated)
```
{
  "ev": "ev-3f2c9d",
  "baseline": {"p95": 184, "p99": 290, "error_rate": "0.12%"},
  "replay": {"p95": 196, "p99": 312, "error_rate": "0.18%"},
  "diff": {"p95_delta_pct": 6.5, "error_rate_delta_pp": 0.06}
}
```
